query: For high-value components operating in aggressive environments, what intervention could improve surface physical and mechanical characteristics? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, the expected improvement relative to an untreated baseline, the conditions under which it should remain effective, prior evidence that would support it, and an experiment whose outcome could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Depositing a protective AlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy (HEA) film via co‐filter cathode vacuum arc deposition (Co-FCVAD) on high‐value components and subsequently annealing it at 800 °C will generate a dense ZrTiO4 composite oxide layer on the surface that substantially improves wear and oxidation resistance in aggressive operating environments.
generation.material_initial_state: Bare or conventionally finished high-value component surfaces that are vulnerable to oxidation, wear, and degradation under high-temperature and corrosive conditions.
generation.intervention: Apply an AlCrTiZrMo HEA film by Co-FCVAD on the component surface followed by an annealing process at 800 °C for 1 hour.
generation.conditions: Aggressive service environments characterized by high operating temperatures in air (and possibly in the presence of corrosive agents), intermittent thermal shocks, and mechanical stresses.
generation.structural_mediator: The formation of a dense, well-adhered ZrTiO4 composite oxide layer within the HEA film matrix.
generation.mechanism: Upon annealing, elements such as Zr and Ti oxidize and interact synergistically within the HEA microstructure to produce a continuous, protective oxide layer. This oxide layer acts as a physical barrier to oxygen and corrosive species while also reinforcing the mechanical integrity of the surface, thereby mitigating oxidation, wear, and tribocorrosion.
generation.predicted_outcome: The treated components will exhibit a significant decrease in oxidation rates, an increase in surface hardness, and improved wear and tribocorrosion resistance compared to untreated surfaces. Key metrics such as lower friction coefficients, reduced wear rates, and minimal oxide layer degradation should be observed under simulated aggressive conditions.
generation.baseline: Untreated components with standard surface finishes, which typically show higher rates of oxidation, wear and reduced mechanical performance when exposed to similar harsh environments.
generation.boundary: The performance benefits are expected to hold under conditions approximating those during annealing (around 800 °C) and in environments with moderately corrosive species; the protective effect may diminish if subjected to temperatures or chemical environments beyond the designed stability range of the ZrTiO4 oxide layer.
generation.uncertainty: While prior studies on similar HEA film systems suggest improved oxidation and mechanical properties, the exact quantitative improvements (e.g., percentage decrease in wear rate or increase in hardness) remain uncertain until validated by experimental results under specific service conditions. Long-term stability under cyclic thermal and mechanical loads also needs further exploration.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of high-value component samples: one set coated with the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film followed by annealing at 800 °C for 1 hour, and a control set with the untreated surface. Expose both sets to simulated aggressive environments involving high-temperature cycling, oxidizing atmospheres, and mechanical wear/tribocorrosion tests over defined time intervals.
measurements: Wear rate (through tribocorrosion or wear tests)
Oxidation rate (by measuring oxide scale thickness or weight gain)
Friction coefficient and other tribological metrics
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the treated samples do not show statistically significant improvements (e.g., lower wear rates, higher hardness, and reduced oxidation) compared to the control samples under identical testing conditions, or if the protective oxide layer degrades prematurely during cyclic tests, then the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

cited_evidence.text: AbstractAlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy (HEA) films with strong amorphization were obtained by co-filter cathode vacuum arc deposition, and the effect of thermal shock on the films was investigated in order to explore the protection mechanism of HEA films against mechanical components in extreme service environments. The results show that after annealing at 800 °C for 1 h, the formation of a dense ZrTiO4 composite oxide layer on the surface actively prevents the oxidation from continuing, so that the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film exhibits excellent oxidation resistance at 800 °C in air. In the friction-corrosion coupling environment, the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film annealed at 800 °C for 1 h shows the best tribocorrosion resistance due to the stable dense microstructure and excellent mechanical properties, and its ΔOCP, COF and wear rate possess the smallest values of 0.055, 0.04 and 1.34 × 10−6 mm−3·N−1·m−1.Keywords: AlCrTiZrMo high-entropy alloy film, thermal shock, oxidation, tribocorrosion

Filter cathode vacuum arc deposition (FCVAD) has sufficient advantages to obtain multi-component films due to its characteristics of magnetic filtration, high ionization rate (100%) and controllable ion types and ion energy. Co-filter cathode vacuum arc deposition (Co-FCVAD) is obtained by designing a multi-channel for particle transport based on FCVAD, which significantly improves the defects of uncontrollable composition and poor quality in the preparation of HEA films [,]. Thus, in order to improve the performance of mechanical components in extreme service environments, the AlCrTiZrMo film system is determined by selecting elements with a large atomic radius difference and excellent corrosion and high temperature performance. In this work, the AlCrTiZrMo HEA film is prepared based on Co-FCVAD. The synergistic interaction between elements at a high temperature in air is discussed, and the changes in microstructure, mechanical properties and tribocorrosion properties of the film after annealing at different temperatures are studied, so as to analyze the protection mechanisms of AlCrTiZrMo HEA films in the simulated scenario of thermal shock.
